title: Sacred sites as refuges for native plant diversity in an urbanized tropical landscape
methods: negative-binomial GLM with AICc model averaging
principal component analysis for predictor reduction
spatial autocorrelation diagnostics (Moran's I, GAM bivariate smooth, NB-GLMM)
Brunner-Munzel rank-order tests with Cliff's delta
building-footprint morphometrics (density, NNI, AWCI, aggregation index)
data_sources: open building footprints (Sirko et al. 2021, continental-scale building detection)
Antananarivo land-cover map (Dupuy et al., CIRAD Dataverse)
Google Earth Engine / Google Earth Pro imagery
POWO, GBIF and Tropicos taxonomic repositories

data_scope.study_area: Antananarivo, Madagascar (18.9185 S, 47.5211 E) and surroundings, ~40 x 40 km, ~1,200-1,600 m a.s.l.
data_scope.analysis_filter: DBH <= 5 cm, height > 5 cm; >95% estimated unassisted recruits
data_scope.transect_size: 40 m2 (10 x 4 m), 1-6 per patch, mean 42.5 individuals per transect
data_scope.administrative_units_screened: 856 Fokontany classified into 4 urban-rural classes (Jenks on % impervious)
data_scope.predictors: 30 candidate variables reduced to 12 (3 UFC PCs >91% variance; 4 SEC incl. socio-economic index PC1 at 71.5%; 5 EL); all VIF < 1.78; 100 m buffers
data_scope.key_effect: expected native richness ~2.0x higher in sacred patches (beta = 0.70 +/- 0.15 SE, P < 0.001 after spatial correction); exotic sacred effect non-significant (beta = 0.09 +/- 0.10, P = 0.34)
data_scope.landscape_gradient: coverage-standardized native richness falls from 34.9 +/- 2.2 to 15.1 +/- 1.8 species from low to high socio-economic index
data_scope.unknowns: total number and area of sacred sites in the region not reported; full vegetation inventory, species list and herbarium scans withheld pending a Malagasy-led botanical publication; sampling coverage per urban class uneven by design
data_scope.data_availability: spatial, predictor and analysis datasets plus code on figshare (10.6084/m9.figshare.29125403)

core_conclusion: Across 329 vegetation patches in Antananarivo, native woody-plant regeneration declines steeply with building density/complexity and socio-economic development while exotic richness shows no consistent urban signal. The strongest positive predictor is cultural rather than biophysical: expected native richness is about twice as high in 32 sacred patches as in 297 non-sacred ones after spatial correction, and seven of the ten most species-rich patches lie on pre-colonial sacred royal hills. Socio-cultural institutions and ancestral fady taboos therefore act as de-facto conservation infrastructure, presenting both opportunities and barriers for tropical urban restoration.
why_it_matters: One of the first comprehensive field assessments of spontaneous urban vegetation in a lower-income Afrotropical city; shows a socio-cultural variable outweighing most urban-form metrics for native diversity; overturns Global-North regularities (no luxury effect, no peri-urban diversity peak, no garden benefit); measures regeneration rather than standing canopy as the resilience signal; and identifies a small, mappable, already socially protected estate of hills as a concrete conservation target.
why_nature: Geographic rebalancing toward under-represented Global-South urban systems; genuinely coupled human-natural framing joining urban form, census socio-economics, pre-colonial settlement history and spiritual taboos; a counter-intuitive claim that generalizes to church forests, sacred groves and churchyards elsewhere in Africa; a defended methodology (AICc averaging, zero-inflation diagnostics, Moran's I and GAM spatial smooths, drop-one confounding audit, coverage-based rarefaction); and an explicit equitable-authorship and inclusion-and-ethics practice with Malagasy co-authors leading fieldwork and taxonomy.
added_value_to_my_research: Explainable ML (GBM+SHAP) and MGWR refit of the 12 predictors -> institutional non-stationarity as an empirical argument for my spatial-prediction work
Building-footprint morphometrics plus fine-tuned geospatial foundation models transferred across Afrotropical cities -> residual maps as an 'institutional residual' detector for unmapped facilities
R2SFCA accessibility to native-biodiversity refugia with a congestion/trampling penalty -> a non-substitutable supply form for my 2SFCA family
Agent-based model of fady compliance decay under urban turnover -> transferable normative-state module for policy-adherence simulation
Physics-informed GNN over a patch dispersal graph with conserved propagule flow -> validated operator for spatiotemporal diffusion in my mobility and health work
